eyebrow: What a real dependency map needs

steps.label: A service catalog
steps.sub: owner, tier, RTO/RPO, and every upstream/downstream dependency, kept current

steps.label: Discovered, not just documented
steps.sub: distributed tracing finds the calls nobody wrote down

steps.label: Transitive closure
steps.sub: blast radius is everything reachable through the graph, not just the first hop

code:
Service catalog entry (as documented):
  checkout -> pricing-service, inventory-service

Distributed trace (as it actually runs):
  checkout -> pricing-service -> tax-rules-service
  checkout -> inventory-service -> legacy-warehouse-db  (undocumented, sync call)
caption: Tracing finds the coupling that never made it into the wiki — and the blast radius includes it either way.

eyebrow: Blast radius is a graph query, not a guess
code:
blast_radius(checkout-db-failure):
  direct:      checkout, order-history
  transitive:  pricing-service, inventory-service,
               tax-rules-service, legacy-warehouse-db,
               notifications (reads order-history)
caption: Before a failover decision ships, the graph tells you everything reachable — not just the one obviously-impacted service.
